title: What else can a herb look like? 15 random herbs beside the shipped one
question: Which herb is the most interesting plant to you? Say in the comment which, if any, look wrong — and what makes the good one good.
context_md:
First look for the **plant trainer** line (a trainer that breeds new species files, herb first).

Each column is one herb, grown **alone** in an outdoor test bed for 20,000 frames, drawn at full daylight. The **three rows are three different worlds** with the same plant — a look that holds down a column is the plant's; one that changes between rows is the weather. Its seedlings are left out of the picture.

Each variant moves five of the shoot's numbers at random (caption). What I measured: the variant explains **76% of the spread in plant size and 66% in leaf share** across these 48 beds, so the trainer can see shape. What I want ignored: **no herb flowers here** except variant 7 — the shipped herb only flowers under the lab's lamps, which is where the trainer will run. And every plant is still a one-pixel stick with speckled leaves; that is fixed in the engine, not in these numbers, and is the next thing the plan addresses.
